8	/// The chat feature's one port — `features/chat/presentation` depends on
9	/// this abstract class only, never `chat/data` (RNF06). Every method but
10	/// [sendMessage] returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (RNF09); [sendMessage]
11	/// alone returns a `Stream` given the SSE nature of its response
12	/// (Boundaries).
13	abstract class ChatRepository {
14	  /// Calls `chat-sessions-list` (`ApiClient.get`, via
15	  /// `ChatRemoteDataSource`) — works offline via the `chat_sessions` Hive
16	  /// box (Code Map): on [Failure.networkOffline]/[Failure.networkTimeout],
17	  /// falls back to a full dump of that box, same "cache fallback"
18	  /// convention `EntriesRepositoryImpl.list()` already uses for its own
19	  /// first/fresh page. Every other [Failure] propagates as `Left`,
20	  /// unmapped (RNF09).
21	  Future<Either<Failure, List<ChatSession>>> listSessions();
22	
23	  /// Calls `chat-sessions-create` (`ApiClient.post`) with no title
24	  /// (Boundaries: "`chat-sessions-create` with no title") — blocked
25	  /// offline per `requirements.md` ("`POST /chat/sessions` — blocked
26	  /// offline"), so unlike [listSessions] there is no cache fallback here:
27	  /// every [Failure], including [Failure.networkOffline], is returned as
28	  /// `Left`, unmapped. On success, persists the new session to the
29	  /// `chat_sessions` Hive box before returning `Right`, same
30	  /// "persist then return" ordering [listSessions] already uses.
31	  Future<Either<Failure, ChatSession>> createSession();
32	
33	  /// Calls `chat-messages-list` (`ApiClient.get`, [sessionId] appended as
34	  /// the one trailing path segment) — works offline via the
35	  /// `chat_messages` Hive box, same cache-fallback convention
36	  /// [listSessions] already uses, filtered to [sessionId] and sorted by
37	  /// `seq` ascending (the backend's own "ordered by seq", `openapi.yaml`).
38	  Future<Either<Failure, List<ChatMessage>>> listMessages(String sessionId);
39	
40	  /// Calls `chat-messages-send` (`ApiClient.postStream`, [sessionId]
41	  /// appended as the one trailing path segment) with `{content}` — the
42	  /// one streaming exception to this port's otherwise all-`Future` shape
43	  /// (Boundaries/RNF09: "every other method returns
44	  /// `Future<Either<Failure, T>>`"). No connectivity resolves immediately
45	  /// to a single `Left(Failure.networkOffline)` emission, never queued
46	  /// (Boundaries) — `ApiClient.postStream`'s own first awaited `Dio.post`
47	  /// call surfaces that failure before any byte streams. A connection that
48	  /// closes without a `done`/`error` SSE event is surfaced as a single
49	  /// trailing `Left(Failure.networkTimeout)` (Design Notes: "the taxonomy
50	  /// has no dedicated 'dropped stream' code"). No local write queue, no
51	  /// Hive persistence of sent messages (Design Notes: chat holds no local
52	  /// write queue for this story).
53	  Stream<Either<Failure, ChatStreamEvent>> sendMessage(
54	    String sessionId,
55	    String content,
56	  );
57	
58	  /// spec-6-3 — calls `chat-messages-retry` (`ApiClient.postStream`,
59	  /// [sessionId] then [userMessageId] appended as the two trailing path
60	  /// segments, `data: const {}`) — regenerates the AI response for an
61	  /// already-persisted user message without re-sending its content
62	  /// (Boundaries: "never a duplicate question"). Same streaming shape and
63	  /// terminal handling as [sendMessage] (SSE events via
64	  /// `ChatRemoteDataSource`'s shared buffer/parse helper); [userMessageId]
65	  /// must be a real, already-persisted user message id — `ChatCubit`
66	  /// itself never calls this with one that's `null` (Boundaries: "Never
67	  /// calling `chat-messages-retry` with no `serverId`"), falling back to
68	  /// [sendMessage] instead in that case.
69	  Stream<Either<Failure, ChatStreamEvent>> retryMessage(
70	    String sessionId,
71	    String userMessageId,
72	  );

   374	/// (RNF09: never throws on a malformed value), same defensive shape
   375	/// `entry_record_card.dart`'s own `_formatTime` already uses.
   376	String _formatTime(String? createdAt) {

   381	  if (local == null) {

16	/// `entries_injection.dart`'s `entriesBoxName` pattern but split in two
17	/// since each caches a structurally different DTO shape.
18	const chatSessionsBoxName = 'chat_sessions';
19	const chatMessagesBoxName = 'chat_messages';

21	/// Registers the `chat` feature into the project's single `get_it`
22	/// instance (`sl`) — mirrors `entries_injection.dart`'s pattern. Called
23	/// from `setupCoreDependencies()` after `Hive.initFlutter()` has already
24	/// run (Code Map), same ordering requirement `registerEntriesFeature()`
25	/// documents for itself.
26	Future<void> registerChatFeature() async {
27	  final sessionsBox = await Hive.openBox<Map>(chatSessionsBoxName);
28	  final messagesBox = await Hive.openBox<Map>(chatMessagesBoxName);
29	  // `instanceName` disambiguates the two `Box<Map>` singletons from each
30	  // other and from `entries_injection.dart`'s own unnamed one — `get_it`
31	  // keys a registration by type + instance name, so three same-typed
32	  // singletons coexist safely.
33	  sl.registerSingleton<Box<Map>>(
34	    sessionsBox,
35	    instanceName: chatSessionsBoxName,
36	  );
37	  sl.registerSingleton<Box<Map>>(
38	    messagesBox,
39	    instanceName: chatMessagesBoxName,
40	  );
41	
42	  sl.registerLazySingleton<ChatRemoteDataSource>(
43	    () => ChatRemoteDataSource(sl<ApiClient>()),
44	  );
45	
46	  sl.registerLazySingleton<ChatRepository>(
47	    () => ChatRepositoryImpl(
48	      remoteDataSource: sl<ChatRemoteDataSource>(),

50	      messagesBox: sl<Box<Map>>(instanceName: chatMessagesBoxName),
51	    ),
52	  );

55	  // app's lifetime, mirroring `capture_injection.dart`'s own
56	  // `record_pkg.AudioRecorder`/`MicRecorder` registration shape.
57	  sl.registerLazySingleton<Connectivity>(Connectivity.new);
58	  sl.registerLazySingleton<ConnectivityWatcher>(
59	    () => ConnectivityPlusWatcher(connectivity: sl<Connectivity>()),
60	  );

63	  // `MeusRegistrosCubit`: long-lived, so a session bootstrapped on one
64	  // visit to Home/Chat survives leaving and returning within the same app

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

input.message:
Implemented spec-6-5 (Proactive Insight Injection & Failure Isolation) per the frozen spec. All production code is written and `fvm flutter analyze` reports zero issues; `pub get` and `build_runner` ran cleanly. Test verification is mostly done but not 100% complete — see "Incomplete/risky" below for exactly what's still unconfirmed and why.

## Files changed

**New (lib):**
- `lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_insight.dart` — `ChatInsight` entity + `InsightTriggerType` enum + `wireValue` extension (`message_count`/`inactivity`).
- `lib/features/chat/domain/insight_trigger_config.dart` — `insightMessageCountThreshold = 5`, `defaultInsightInactivityTimeout = Duration(minutes: 2)`.
- `lib/features/chat/data/models/insight_dto.dart` (+ generated `.g.dart`) — DTO for `chat-insight-create`'s response.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/widgets/insight_card.dart` — the ochre-spine "INSIGHT" card.

**Modified (lib):**
- `chat_repository.dart` — added `generateInsight(sessionId, {triggerType, triggerKey})`.
- `chat_remote_data_source.dart` — added `generateInsight` calling `chat-insight-create`.
- `chat_repository_impl.dart` — added `generateInsight`: pure passthrough, maps `status=='ready' && content!=null` to `ChatInsight`, else `Right(null)`; `Left` unmapped.
- `chat_state.dart` — `ChatReady.activeInsight` (nullable `ChatInsight`, default null), `copyWith` extended.
- `chat_cubit.dart` — the core: ctor gains optional `insightInactivityTimeout` (test seam, defaults to the real 2-minute constant, no DI change needed); new fields `_insightTimeout`, `_insightMessagesSinceWindowStart`, `_insightInactivityTimer`, `_insightTriggerKey`, `_insightWindowCounter`; `_resetInsightWindow`/`_restartInsightInactivityTimer`/`_fireInsightTrigger`/`_generateInsight`/`_applyInsightResult`/`dismissInsight` added; wired into `sendMessage()` (counter/threshold check right after the `_isSending` guard) and the 3 bootstrap/switchSession/startNewSession `ChatReady(...)` sites; `close()` cancels the timer.
- `chat_screen.dart` — interleaves `InsightCard` as the trailing `ListView` item when `activeInsight != null`.
- `design_tokens.dart` — 4 new tokens: `chatInsightSpineWidth`, `chatInsightCardPadding`, `chatInsightLabelSpacing`, `chatInsightDismissIconSize`.

**New/extended (test):**
- Extended `chat_remote_data_source_test.dart`, `chat_repository_impl_test.dart` (generateInsight call shape, status→entity mapping, Left propagation).
- Extended `chat_cubit_test.dart` with a full `proactive insight — spec-6-5` group (fires at 5th message, fires after injected-short inactivity, never-both/never-twice, fire-and-forget, failure isolation for both Left and non-ready Right, drop-on-session-switch, dismiss clears without touching other fields, dismiss-with-none-active no-op, reset on switchSession/startNewSession, timer cancelled on close()).
- New `insight_card_test.dart` (label/content/spine color, dismiss tap, 44pt tap target, button semantics).
- Extended `chat_screen_test.dart` with two widget tests (card renders as trailing item via 5 real sends; dismiss tap wires to `dismissInsight()`).

## A real cross-cutting issue I found and fixed

Starting a real `Timer` on every `ChatCubit` bootstrap broke `testWidgets`' `!timersPending` invariant check in **every other test file that bootstraps a `ChatCubit`** (`app_router_test.dart`, `app_drawer_test.dart`, `main_test.dart`, plus my own `chat_screen_test.dart` additions) — ~60 `testWidgets` blocks total. I confirmed empirically that neither `addTearDown` nor group-level `tearDown()` run early enough to cancel the timer before that check fires (it runs *inside* `testWidgets`' own callback execution). The fix I applied in all 4 files: shadow the real `testWidgets` (`import '...flutter_test.dart' hide testWidgets` + a local wrapper that closes the relevant `ChatCubit`(s) in a `finally` block after the real callback). Verified working for `chat_screen_test.dart` (16/16 pass, including the 2 new spec-6-5 tests). The same pattern was applied to the other 3 files but **I could not get a clean confirming test run** for them — see below.

## Verified
- `fvm flutter pub get` — resolves, no conflicts.
- `fvm flutter pub run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs` — `insight_dto.g.dart` generated cleanly.
- `fvm flutter analyze` — **zero issues**, full repo.
- `fvm flutter test test/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen_test.dart` — **16/16 pass**.
- Ran the full suite once before the testWidgets-wrapper fix: confirmed exactly the predicted failure set (pending-timer assertions) and nothing else new/unrelated.

## Incomplete / risky — needs a follow-up full test run
After applying the `testWidgets`-wrapper fix to `app_router_test.dart`, `app_drawer_test.dart`, and `main_test.dart`, I could not get a clean re-run to complete: the sandbox accumulated multiple concurrent/stale `flutter_tester`/`dart` processes (some left over from earlier timed-out runs) and subsequent `fvm flutter test` invocations stalled with near-zero CPU progress for several minutes — looks like contention on a shared `.dart_tool`/build-cache lock, not a logic hang in the code itself (I reasoned through the actual timer/zone mechanics and don't see a plausible infinite loop in my changes). I was not permitted to kill the stray processes (sandbox denied `pkill`). **Before considering this story done, please run `fvm flutter test` once on a clean machine/process state** to confirm:
1. `app_router_test.dart`, `app_drawer_test.dart`, `main_test.dart` pass with the new `testWidgets` wrapper (logic verified by inspection and by the identical pattern working in `chat_screen_test.dart`, but not re-confirmed after the latest edits to those 3 files).
2. The new `chat_cubit_test.dart` insight-group tests pass (plain `test()`, not `testWidgets`, so unaffected by the timer issue above — these are pure async/`Future.delayed` based, not fake_async, consistent with the spec's "no fake_async dependency" constraint).
3. `chat_repository_impl_test.dart`/`chat_remote_data_source_test.dart` extensions pass (straightforward mocktail stubs, low risk).

## Design decisions worth flagging
- `InsightCard`'s ochre spine is rendered via a plain colored `Container` bar inside an `IntrinsicHeight`+`Row`, clipped by the outer card's `Clip.antiAlias`, rather than a `BoxDecoration.border` (a single-sided border + `borderRadius` renders unreliably in Flutter) — this is within the spec's "implementer's choice" allowance.
- `InsightDto.errorCode`/`content`/`dismissedAt` are all `String?` (nullable) even though the spec's prose groups `triggerType`/`status`/`errorCode` as "all raw String" — I made `errorCode` nullable because the contract marks it `nullable: true` and a `'ready'` response always carries a null `errorCode`; a non-nullable field would throw on decode.
- No changes were made to `chat_injection.dart` (DI) — correct per spec, since the constructor's new parameter is optional with the real default.

No AGENTS.md boundaries were touched (no `docs/input/` edits, no design tokens outside `design_tokens.dart`, no extension features, RF10's shared-use-case rule untouched, domain layer still imports neither Flutter nor data).
